a little about me

Who I am

I am Hilda Samukelo Sofala, a software engineering student based in Johannesburg.

Right now I am on the Software Engineering Learnership at WeThinkCode_. I write Python and Java, work on command-line applications in teams, and learn how to test and debug code.

I am also a Work Readiness Supervisor there. I run professional development workshops for 50+ learners and coach my peers on public speaking, interview preparation and professional communication.

Outside of class I volunteer with GDG Soweto. I have come second at the Mukuru SheHacks - WeThinkCode_ Hackathon and been named an honourable winner at Canvathon.

Projects I have contributed to

Java school project, done in a team

Robot World

Our team built a Java application using object-oriented programming, and I contributed to developing and testing it. The work covered classes, inheritance, exceptions, commands, movement logic, JSON communication and automated tests, with Maven for builds and tests and Git and GitHub for version control.

When something broke, I debugged by tracing command responses and implementation logic.

JavaOOPMavenJSONAutomated testsGit and GitHub

Solo, Python QA project

BIM File Security System - QA

An automated test suite that checks the BIM File Security System from the outside. It is built around written requirements with unique IDs, and every test is tagged with the requirement it verifies, so each one can be traced to a test.

It covers logging in with valid, wrong, empty and injection-style input, what each role (architect, engineer, contractor and client) can view and edit, files that must be stored encrypted and rejected if tampered with, and sessions that end on logout and expire when idle.

PythonpytestTest automationRequirement traceabilitySecurity testing

School project, existing codebase, done in a team

Brownfields Project

As a team, we worked on an existing codebase, and I learned its structure before making any changes. I contributed bug fixes and new features, and we wrote and ran tests to confirm that nothing already working had broken. We used Git and GitHub for version control throughout.
